On Fri, Oct 30, 2026 at 08:35 AM kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — incoming high-priority customer escalation from Acme...

Quick triage summary (what we see right now):
- 429s correlate with saturated model-serving shards in us-west1; autoscaler lagging ~90s on burst traffic.
- 5xx spikes coincide with increased queue depths on a subset of GPU nodes (OOM/retry boundary).
- Client retry behavior: many clients (including Acme) retry aggressively with short backoff leading to a retry storm that amplifies load.

Immediate mitigations we applied (08:50-08:57):
1) Raised request concurrency limit for Acme routes and added temporary capacity (spin up two additional ded instances in us-west1).
2) Applied a soft circuit-breaker: reject with 429 + Retry-After for excessive per-client QPS to break retry loops.
3) Implemented temporary larger KV cache for hot prefixes to reduce model compute on repeated sequences.

Observable impact: error rates dropped ~65% in 10min; latency improved for sampled traces. We still see tail timeouts on long sequences.

Next steps (short):
- Confirm with Acme that customer-side retry/backoff has been throttled. Marissa, can you ask them to push a canary with exponential backoff?
- Follow up with infra on autoscaler tuning and faster scale-up for short bursts.

I’ll post a full postmortem draft after we stabilize.

—Rishi
Dist. Eng Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Subject: Draft postmortem & prioritized remediation list (for review)

Team — drafting the postmortem for Acme incident (Oct 30). Key items:

Incident summary:
- Timeline: 07:45–09:10 PT spike in 5xx/429 with retry amplification causing degraded checkout success rates.
- Root causes: autoscaler scale-up delay for short bursts, missing alerting on retry amplification, and client retry configuration that lacked exponential backoff.

Primary follow-up actions (owners + ETA):
1) Alerting gap: create a "retry amplification" alert (SRE) — Owner: Jonas — ETA: 2 weeks.
2) Runbooks: write an ops runbook for circuit-breaker toggles and emergency capacity adds — Owner: Rishi — ETA: 1 week.
3) SLO tuning: re-evaluate per-route latency SLOs and add burst capacity reserve policy for high-rev customers — Owner: Hannah — ETA: 3 weeks.
4) Canary tests: add synthetic canaries that simulate retry storms to validate autoscaler behavior — Owner: Marissa/Infra — ETA: 4 weeks.
5) Customer communication template + credit approach: propose 5%-10% service credit for impacted window — Owner: Kimberly — ETA: 2 days for proposal.

Questions for leadership:
- Do we want to pre-approve a standard credit band for similar incidents?
- Should we accelerate a permanent autoscaler improvement (work effort ~3 wks) vs. keep as backlog?

Draft postmortem link: https://drive.redwood.internal/Acme/incident-20261030 (internal).

—Hannah
Head of Reliability | Redwood Inference

Subject: Acme incident 10/30 — remediation summary and next steps

Alice,

First, sincere apologies for the disruption on Oct 30. We understand checkouts were impacted and appreciate your patience. Summary of what happened and what we’re doing: 

What happened: transient traffic burst saturated a subset of model-serving shards; autoscaler scale-up lagged and combined with aggressive client retries produced a retry amplification loop that caused elevated 5xx/429 and timeouts.

What we did to mitigate:
- Added temporary capacity and applied a soft circuit-breaker to break retry loops (applied 08:50 PT).
- Increased per-route concurrency for Acme and tuned KV cache for hot prefixes.
- Worked with your ops team to run a canary with exponential backoff; observed reduced amplification.

Remediation plan & commitments:
- We will publish a public runbook for emergency circuit breaker and capacity adds (ETA: 1 week).
- Implement a "retry amplification" alert and improve autoscaler scale-up behavior for bursts (ETA: 2 weeks for alert, 3 weeks for autoscaler improvement).
- Re-evaluate per-route SLOs and introduce a burst-reserve policy for high-value customers (ETA: 3 weeks).
- We propose a 7% service credit for the impacted billing window while legal/finance finalizes wording.

Links: incident notes and postmortem draft: https://drive.redwood.internal/Acme/incident-20261030

We want to schedule a 30-minute postmortem review with your team next week to walk through the technical details and remediation plan. What times work for you?

Again — very sorry. We take this seriously and will follow up with the agreed remediation and the runbook.

Best,
Kimberly Park
VP, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
